title: Pushing the tempo to keep the band awake
summary: Greer raised the tempo a notch to keep the men alert.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Was that the way when you -- when the band was a little bit tired you'd spark the tempo up just a little bit?

Just a trifle. Just enough to make it exciting. Anything, I didn't care what it was, I'd pick it up just a notch and keep them guys alert through the first show then they could relax you know. And the guys would all curse me out, man. "Man, why you do that?" I'd say, "Well, I go home early and go to sleep." I ain't saw no bed.
Duke was looking at me. Man, I think that's how he started playing the piano with his back to the audience. You saw Duke?

Was his back to the audience? He would be playing the piano and yawning. And I would whistle down, "Wake up, you so and so. Man, come on, let's take it." But I love him. That was my guy, baby. And the whole band was my guys.
My job, like I told you, was to keep the band on a level ke Because all bands, they would start low and accelerate, you know. But our band, with all them stars, smooth as velvet.
How did you -- do you have anything
you recall about Chicago you wanted to say before I interrupted you about the tempo?
